people: Alfred Hayes (President, Federal Reserve Bank of New York, 1956-1975)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Alfred Hayes began his banking career in 1933 as an analyst in the investment department of the City Bank Farmers Trust Company, transferred seven years later to the bond department of the National City Bank, and joined the New York Trust Company in 1942 as an assistant secretary in the investment department. The page states he came to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from the New York Trust Company, where he had been vice president in charge of the foreign division between 1949 and 1956. He was named president of the New York Fed and vice chairman of the Federal Open Market Committee on August 1, 1956. The page states that Hayes retired from the New York Fed on August 1, 1975, and joined Morgan Stanley International Inc. as chairman in November 1975, and was named chairman emeritus in 1981. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: New York Trust Company to New York Fed presidency, then New York Fed to Morgan Stanley International as chairman

people: Allan Sproul (President, Federal Reserve Bank of New York, 1941-1956)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Allan Sproul served as president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from January 1941 to June 1956, and was named vice chairman of the Federal Open Market Committee in 1942. The page states that in 1956 he resigned from the New York Fed and returned to California to serve as a director of Wells Fargo Bank. The page also records that he served as a director of Kaiser Aluminum and Chemical Corporation. Sproul died in 1978. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: New York Fed presidency to a directorship at Wells Fargo Bank

people: Jeffrey M. Bucher (Governor, Board of Governors, 1972-1976)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that from 1957 to 1972 Jeffrey Bucher worked for the 1st Interstate Bank of California, serving as its senior vice president from 1969 until his appointment to the Board of Governors on June 5, 1972. He served as a governor until his resignation on January 2, 1976. The page states that after leaving the Board he served on the board of directors of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank of California, as a trustee of Mortgage and Realty Trust in Philadelphia, as a director of Manufacturers Bank in Los Angeles from 1978 to 1980, as chairman of First Interstate Bank of Washington from 1983 to 1987, and as a member of the board of directors of Mizuho Corporate Bank of California. From 2001 to 2009 he was a member of the board of directors of MCG Capital Corporation, serving as chairman from 2007 to 2009. The page also records law-firm roles at Pepper, Hamilton & Scheetz, Bryan Cave LLP, Lillick & Charles LLP and Kozusko Lahey Harris LLP, and teaching roles. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: 1st Interstate Bank of California to the Board of Governors, then on to bank boards and chairmanships including First Interstate Bank of Washington

people: Lyle E. Gramley (Governor, Board of Governors, 1980-1985)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Lyle E. Gramley served on the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System from May 28, 1980, until September 1, 1985, having earlier worked at the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City and as director of the Board's Division of Research and Statistics. The page states that after leaving the Board he accepted a position as chief economist at the Mortgage Bankers Association of America; in 2002 he became a senior economic adviser at the Schwab Washington Research Group; in 2007 he joined Soleil Securities Corporation; and he served as a senior adviser at Potomac Research Group in Washington, DC. He died in 2015. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: Board of Governors to the Schwab Washington Research Group and Soleil Securities Corporation

people: Lawrence K. Roos (President, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, 1976-1983)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that in the 1950s and early 1960s Lawrence K. Roos worked as a commercial banker and bank executive, and that before joining the St. Louis Fed he worked at the First National Bank of St. Louis, where he was an executive. He became president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis on March 22, 1976, and retired January 31, 1983. The page states that after retiring from the Bank in 1983 Roos took a position at the investment banking firm Bear, Stearns and Company as a special limited partner, where he was an economic adviser on monetary policy, citing a New York Times report of January 20, 1983. He died in 2005. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: First National Bank of St. Louis to the St. Louis Fed presidency, then on to Bear, Stearns and Company

people: Darryl R. Francis (President, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, 1966-1976)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Darryl R. Francis began his career at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis in 1944 as an agricultural economist, and that from 1949 until 1953 he was employed as a commercial banker in Memphis and later served as a vice president at Boatmen's National Bank in St. Louis. He rejoined the St. Louis Fed as a vice president in 1953, became first vice president in 1959, and became president on January 17, 1966, retiring February 29, 1976. The page states that before his retirement he also served as chairman of Merchants Bank in Fort Smith, Arkansas. He died in 2002. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: Boatmen's National Bank and Memphis commercial banking to the St. Louis Fed presidency; chairman of Merchants Bank, Fort Smith

people: Robert P. Mayo (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, 1970-1981)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Robert Mayo was a career executive at the US Treasury from 1941 to 1960, and that he left the US Treasury in August 1960 to become vice president of Continental Illinois National Bank and Trust Company of Chicago, concentrating on trust investments and public affairs. The page states he left Chicago in 1968 to become director of the Bureau of the Budget, was appointed counselor to President Nixon on July 1, 1970, and left later that month to become president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, serving from July 29, 1970, to July 1, 1981. He died in 2003. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: Continental Illinois National Bank and Trust Company of Chicago into federal service and then the Chicago Fed presidency

people: Roger W. Ferguson Jr. (Governor 1997-1999 and Vice Chair 1999-2006, Board of Governors)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Roger W. Ferguson Jr. joined the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System on November 5, 1997, was appointed vice chairman on October 5, 1999, and resigned from Board service on April 28, 2006. The page states that after resigning from the Board, Ferguson became chairman of Swiss Re America Holding Corporation and a member of Swiss Re's executive board, and was also appointed head of financial services and a member of Swiss Re's Executive Committee. The page states that in 2008 he became president and chief executive officer of the TIAA-CREF. It also records that from 1981 to 1984 he was an attorney at Davis Polk & Wardwell and from 1984 to 1987 a partner at McKinsey & Company, Inc. No ethics finding is recorded.

people: W. Braddock Hickman (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, 1963-1970)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that W. Braddock Hickman was supervisor of economic studies at New York Life Insurance Company from 1953 to 1956 before joining American Airlines as director of economic research and then assistant vice president. The page states he was appointed senior vice president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland in 1960 and was named president in 1963, serving from May 1963 until his death in office in 1970. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: New York Life Insurance Company into the Cleveland Fed

people: Mark W. Olson (Governor, Board of Governors, 2001-2006)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Mark W. Olson joined First Bank System, now US Bancorp, and was named as an officer in 1969, and that in 1976 he was named president and chief executive officer of Security State Bank in Fergus Falls, Minnesota, a bank his father had been the lead organizer in chartering in 1957. The page states he was elected president of the American Bankers Association in 1986, and from 1988 to 1999 served as national director of Ernst & Young LLP's regulatory consulting practice for the financial services industry, before becoming staff director of the US Senate Banking Committee's Securities Subcommittee in 2000. He was sworn in as a member of the Board of Governors on December 7, 2001, and left on June 30, 2006. The page states he then became chairman of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, and in September 2009 joined Corporate Risk Advisors LLC as cochairman. He died in 2018. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: First Bank System and Security State Bank into the Board of Governors

people: Joseph A. Erickson (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, 1948-1961)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that in 1920 Joseph A. Erickson began his long association with National Shawmut Bank in Boston, beginning as a clerk, being promoted to manager of the Credit Department in 1925 and to branch manager in 1926, becoming a vice president in 1928 and being elevated to executive vice president in 1942. The page states that in 1948 he was appointed president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, becoming its eighth president in December 1948 and serving until February 1961. He died in 1983. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: National Shawmut Bank executive vice presidency to the Boston Fed presidency

people: Robert P. Forrestal (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, 1983-1996)
summary: Federal Reserve History states that Robert P. Forrestal became president and chief executive officer of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta on December 7, 1983, and served until January 1, 1996. The page states that after retiring from the Bank he worked with the Atlanta law firm of Smith, Gambrell & Russell and served on several corporate boards, and that he was a member of the boards of directors of Equifax Inc., Genuine Parts Co., ING North America Co., and the ING Advisory Council in the Netherlands. He died in 2004. No ethics finding is recorded.
move: Atlanta Fed presidency to the board of ING North America and the ING Advisory Council
